title: About the CISA exam
description: What the exam looks like, how to book it, what happens on the day and after, and how passing turns into certification. Written in plain language by KaiSip from ISACA's and PSI's published information.
disclaimer: KaiSip is an independent study app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by ISACA. CISA is a registered trademark of ISACA, used here only to describe the exam. ISACA alone sets the exam rules and decides eligibility and certification. No study app can promise a pass, including this one.
check_before_booking: Fees, rules and requirements on this page were checked on the date shown. They can change, so check isaca.org before you book.

sections.title: The exam at a glance
sections.summary: A 4-hour, computer-based exam of 150 multiple-choice questions, scored on a scale from 200 to 800. A score of 450 or higher passes.
items: 150 multiple-choice questions in 4 hours (240 minutes). Each question has four options and one best answer.
Some questions may share a short scenario, so you read the setup once and use it for more than one question.
Scores are scaled from 200 (the lowest) to 800 (every scored question answered correctly). You pass with 450 or more.
Scaling keeps different versions of the exam comparable, so 450 is not a fixed percentage of questions.
Some questions are unscored pretest items. Treat every question as if it counts.
There is no penalty for a wrong answer, so answer every question.
Your results include a breakdown by domain. It is for your information only and does not change your score.
Languages: English, Simplified Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean and Spanish.
You take it on a computer, either at a PSI test center or online with a remote proctor from PSI.
The current content outline took effect on August 1, 2024.

sources.label: ISACA support: how the exam is scored

sections.title: The five domains and their weights
sections.summary: ISACA's content outline splits the exam into five domains. A domain's weight is its share of the exam, so it is a good guide to where your study time goes.

domains.name: Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Implementation
Information Systems Operations and Business Resilience

items: Domains 4 and 5 together make up just over half the exam, so give them the most practice time.
Domain 3 is the smallest at 12%, yet roughly one question in eight still comes from it. Don't skip it.
Domain 1 is the IS auditor's method. Its ideas, such as independence, evidence and risk-based scope, show up in every domain.
Read every question as the IS (information systems) auditor unless it tells you otherwise.

sections.title: Registering and fees
sections.summary: You register and pay through your ISACA account, then book a date with PSI. You have 6 months from registering to sit the exam.
steps: Create an ISACA account. Use your name exactly as it appears on the ID you will bring on exam day.
Register for the exam and pay. You can register at any time of year.
Your 6-month eligibility period starts on the day you register.
Starting 48 hours after you pay, book your date with PSI through your ISACA account. Dates open up to 90 days ahead.
items: Exam fee: US$575 for ISACA members, US$760 for non-members. Your price depends on whether you are a member when you register.
Membership is optional. Professional membership is US$145 a year, plus dues for your local chapter where one exists; chapter dues vary and are added at checkout.
Recent graduate membership is US$68 a year and student membership US$25.
Reschedule for free up to 48 hours before your appointment. Within 48 hours, you either sit the exam or lose the fee.

Need more time? You can buy one 6-month extension for US$75. It shows on your dashboard from 30 days before to 30 days after your window ends. If you have a booked date, cancel it at least 48 hours ahead before you buy.
Fees are not refunded and cannot be transferred. If your window ends before you sit the exam, the fee is lost.
If you miss your appointment or arrive more than 15 minutes late, you also lose the fee.

For a genuine hardship, such as sudden illness, a death in your immediate family or a traffic accident, contact PSI within 72 hours after the missed appointment, with documents. If PSI declines, you register and pay again.

sections.title: Test center or online
sections.summary: You can take it at a test center or online. A test center gives you a prepared room; online saves travel but puts the setup on you. Follow ISACA's guide and your check-in specialist; ask ISACA support if unsure.
items: Test center: PSI provides the computer, and lockers hold your belongings. Plan your route and arrive at least 30 minutes early.
Online: you need a computer with a webcam, a working microphone and a stable internet connection.
Use your own computer if you can. ISACA strongly recommends a personal one: work computers often block the exam software, and if a work computer fails on exam day, you pay to retake.
The webcam and microphone must stay on for the whole exam. Headphones, headsets and earbuds are not allowed.
Use one screen. Unplug extra monitors, cameras and microphones before you start.
Turn off any VPN and avoid a work network; both can block the secure connection. You need administrator rights to install the exam software.
Phones, virtual machines and most tablets cannot run the exam, and some editions of Windows are not supported. Check PSI's list before you book.
PSI asks for at least 8 GB of memory (16 GB recommended) and recommends 3 Mbps or faster up and down. A wired connection is steadier than Wi-Fi.
Sit alone in a private room with a door you can close. Expect a 360-degree room scan, a desk scan, a floor-to-ceiling scan and a mirror check.

ISACA's guide lets you scan the room with your phone through a QR code, while PSI's page says a phone is only for your photo ID. Follow ISACA's guide and your check-in specialist; ask ISACA support if unsure.
Chat with the remote proctor is in English only.
steps: Before you book, run PSI's compatibility check on the computer and network you will actually use.
Read PSI's current computer requirements, because supported systems change.
After booking, run the Secure Browser tutorial under My Tests in PSI's portal. PSI says it is the only complete check of your setup.
On the day, restart, close other programs and press Launch at least 15 minutes early so the PSI Secure Browser can download.
Check-in opens 30 minutes before your appointment.

sections.title: Exam day
sections.summary: Bring one valid ID, arrive or log in early, and leave everything else behind.
items: Bring one current, original, government-issued ID showing your name, photo and signature. Copies, handwritten IDs and digital IDs are not accepted.
Your first and last name must match your registration. Without valid ID you cannot sit the exam, and you lose the fee.
Test center: arrive at least 30 minutes early. Online: check-in opens 30 minutes before your start time.
More than 15 minutes late counts as a missed appointment, and the fee is lost.
Nothing comes in with you: no notes or paper, calculator, phone, smartwatch, smart glasses, headphones or bag, and no food or drink, not even water.
You may take up to two breaks of up to 10 minutes each, with the proctor's permission. The exam clock keeps running.
Online: keep facing the screen, since looking away is not allowed, and have no food, drink or gum at the desk.
Pace: 240 minutes for 150 questions is 96 seconds a question. Answer every one; a blank earns nothing.

sources.label: ISACA support: what to bring on exam day

sections.title: After the exam
sections.summary: A preliminary pass or fail shows on screen when you finish. The official result follows within 10 business days.
items: Your official score arrives by email and in your MyISACA account within 10 business days.
Results show your scaled score and how you did by domain. They do not show which questions you got wrong.
If you did not pass, you can ask for a rescore in writing through ISACA support within 30 days of your results. The fee is US$75.
Retakes: up to four attempts in the 12 months from your first. Wait 30 days before the second attempt, then 90 days before each later one. Each attempt costs the full fee.
If you pass, you cannot sit the same exam again during your 5-year window to apply.
Passing is not the same as being certified. You still need to apply, as the next section explains.

sections.title: Becoming and staying certified
sections.summary: After passing, you apply with proof of work experience, then keep the certification current with yearly learning and a fee. ISACA decides every application.
steps: Wait for your official score, then apply within 5 years of passing.
Show 5 years of work experience in information systems (IS) audit, control, assurance or security, in at least one CISA domain, gained within the 10 years before you apply.
Ask a supervisor, manager, colleague or client to verify your experience. Family members and human resources (HR) staff cannot verify it.
Agree to ISACA's Code of Professional Ethics and its IS audit and assurance standards, and pay the US$50 application fee. Processing takes about 2 to 3 weeks.
items: Waivers can replace up to 3 of the 5 years. At least 2 years must be direct audit, control, assurance or security experience.
Waivers on the current application: associate degree, 1 year; bachelor's, master's or doctorate in any field, 2 years; master's in information systems or a related field, 3 years.

Full Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA) certification or Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) member status counts for 2 years. Only one education waiver can be applied.
General IS or general audit work can count for 1 year: 1 continuous year with one employer, not overlapping your main experience.
ISACA support also lists a 1-year waiver for ISACA's IT Audit Fundamentals certificate or the Certificate of Cloud Auditing Knowledge (CCAK). Confirm it with ISACA before you rely on it.

CISA Associate: for students who pass through an ISACA academic partner program but lack the experience. It needs active ISACA membership, a one-time US$25 fee and an application within 6 months of passing.
The Associate title lasts up to 4 years, or until you have the experience, and needs no continuing professional education (CPE).
Keeping CISA: earn at least 20 CPE hours a year and 120 over each 3-year cycle, starting January 1 of the year after you certify.
At least 90 of the 120 cycle hours must relate to the CISA content outline; up to 30 can be other professional development.
Annual maintenance fee: US$45 for members, US$85 for non-members, due by January 1.
ISACA audits a random sample of CPE records each year, and not complying can cost you the certification.
Keep your CPE evidence for at least 3 years. ISACA's pages do not agree on the period, so check the current CPE policy and keep it for the longer one.
